A stub that never calls the builder satisfies AC #1's text while the risky new code path — builder registration, profile override injection, endpoint wiring — never executes in CI, violating E6(f).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC #1; Testing section
scenarios: An executor uses a unittest mock to stub `_pai_structured`, constructs the config, and asserts the env vars are readable — the assertion passes, AC #1 is ticked, but the builder is never invoked and the profile override is never applied.
CI stays green on a machine without a running local server; the builder's ImportError guard and URL wiring are never exercised.

findings.finding: When REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=anthropic (or any non-openai provider) is set together with REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL, the plan's new _pai_check_config no longer raises, the openai builder is not registered (gated on base_url AND provider=openai), and the anthropic builder ignores cfg.base_url entirely — so the user's REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL is silently dropped without any warning. This recreates the original silent-drop problem for the anthropic+base_url combination, in the same direction the story is fixing for openai+base_url.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a validation rule in `_pai_check_config` that, when `api_key` is non-empty AND `base_url` resolves to a non-loopback host, either enforces an `https://` scheme or emits an explicit advisory warning — and cover this with a named test in `tests/unit/test_openai_compatible_provider.py`.

Plan example uses `http://localhost:1234/v1` (loopback, safe) but the contrast test uses a non-loopback `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` without specifying scheme

ABSENCE: no plan section specifies scheme validation or warns on plaintext HTTP to a remote host when api_key is non-empty
findings.finding: The plan's `_pai_check_config` validation performs an absolute-URL check on `base_url` but does not enforce HTTPS for non-loopback addresses where a real `api_key` is present. A real operator credential (`api_key`) could be transmitted in plaintext over HTTP to a remote endpoint (e.g. a vLLM proxy or LiteLLM gateway on a non-loopback host), crossing a network boundary without encryption.
findings.location: Approach section — `_pai_check_config` validation spec; Testing section — failure paths; AC line `_pai_check_config` no longer raises for a valid `base_url`
scenarios: Operator sets `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL=http://remote-vllm-host.internal/v1` with a real `api_key` (e.g. a LiteLLM master key); the api_key travels in plaintext over the internal network
A misconfigured `http://` instead of `https://` for a hosted endpoint silently downgrades transport security without any warning from rebar
findings.suggested_fix: In `_pai_check_config`, after the absolute-URL check, parse the URL with `urllib.parse.urlparse`; if `parsed.hostname` is not a loopback address (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`) and `parsed.scheme != 'https'` and `api_key` is non-empty (not the placeholder), raise `LLMConfigError` with a message such as: 'REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL uses plaintext HTTP with a non-loopback host and a real api_key — use https:// or omit the key for an unauthenticated local server.'

Future contributors hitting the `_builders` dict or the profile override will have no canonical record of why the pattern exists, making it likely to be undone or duplicated incorrectly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly document ProviderSession's lifecycle (per-call vs shared singleton) in the plan and, if it is or could be shared, ensure `_builders` mutation is atomic (e.g. build a fresh dict per session rather than mutating a shared one).
evidence: Plan says 'the openai builder is registered ONLY when cfg.base_url is set' implying a conditional write to `_builders`
Plan does not state whether ProviderSession is per-call or shared across calls
No lock or copy-on-write is mentioned for the `_builders` dict mutation
findings.finding: The plan does not specify `ProviderSession`'s sharing/lifecycle model. If `ProviderSession` is reused across concurrent requests (e.g. a module-level singleton or cached instance), the conditional write to `_builders` ('registered ONLY when `cfg.base_url` is set') is a check-then-act on mutable shared state with no locking mentioned — one request with `base_url` could register the builder while a concurrent request without `base_url` reads a partially-mutated dict.
findings.location: 'WHEN the openai builder is registered' subsection; Scope: providers.py
scenarios: ProviderSession is instantiated once per process (singleton): thread A serving a base_url request registers the builder; thread B serving a bare openai request reads _builders mid-mutation and gets inconsistent state
ProviderSession is per-call: no race, but this lifecycle is never asserted in the plan, leaving the assumption implicit and fragile
findings.suggested_fix: If ProviderSession is constructed per-call (per `run()` invocation), state this explicitly in a comment at the class definition so future contributors don't accidentally make it a singleton.
